title: Nash blowups
summary: The Nash blowup and the normalised Nash blowup of a reduced finite-type k-scheme of pure dimension d with dense smooth locus, built intrinsically from the Grassmannian of rank-d quotients of Ω_{X/k}: universal property, modification property, locality, field base change, the Gauss-map and blowup descriptions, the triviality criterion (ν iso iff Ω has a locally free rank-d quotient), Nobile's theorem in characteristic zero, the Duarte–Núñez-Betancourt theorem for normal schemes over perfect fields of characteristic p, the criteria for the normalised blowup, and the never-resolves principle for the two iterations.

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.coherentGrassmannian.mapOfSurjective

layers.title: The setting and the Nash modification of a sheaf

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setting
targets.statement: For X reduced and locally of finite type over k: X_sm is dense iff X is geometrically reduced; over a perfect field X_sm is dense; if X_sm is dense it contains every generic point and meets every component densely; if moreover X is pure of dimension d, X_sm = X_sm^{(d)} and Ω_{X/k}|_{X_sm} is finite locally free of rank d.
hypotheses: X reduced, locally of finite type over k
for the last clause, X pure of dimension d

tests.name: setting_inseparable_point

tests.name: setting_dualNumbers

tests.name: setting_mixed_dimension

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nashModification
targets.statement: For a scheme X, a quasi-coherent O_X-module F of finite type, r : ℕ and an open U with F|_U finite locally free of rank r, N(X, F, r, U) is the scheme-theoretic image of the classifying map σ_U : U → Gr_r(F) of the identity quotient of F|_U, with π_N : N → X the restriction of the Grassmannian's structure map.
hypotheses: X a scheme (reduced and locally Noetherian for the API)
U open with F|_U finite locally free of rank r (dense for the API)

api.name: nashModification.isClosedImmersion
api.statement: N → Gr_r(F) is a closed immersion, N is reduced, and its support is the closure of σ_U(U)

api.name: nashModification.isIso_over
api.statement: π_N restricts to an isomorphism π_N⁻¹(U) → U, and π_N⁻¹(U) is dense in N

api.name: nashModification.eq_of_le
api.statement: for a dense open U' ⊆ U, N(X, F, r, U') = N(X, F, r, U) as closed subschemes of Gr_r(F)

api.name: nashModification.quotient
api.statement: the universal quotient restricts to a locally free rank-r quotient π_N^*F → L_F, the identity quotient over U

api.name: nashModification.isProper
api.statement: π_N is proper

tests.name: nashModification_locallyFree
tests.statement: if F is finite locally free of rank r on X then N ≅ X

tests.name: nashModification_torsion_summand
tests.statement: for O ⊕ O/(x) on 𝔸¹, r = 1, U = D(x): the Grassmannian fibre over 0 is ℙ¹ but N ≅ 𝔸¹ with L_F = O

tests.name: nashModification_maximalIdeal
tests.statement: for the ideal of the origin in 𝔸², r = 1, U = 𝔸² ∖ 0: N is the blowup of the origin, N ≠ X

tests.name: nashModification_not_whole_grassmannian
tests.statement: the whole Grassmannian (fibre ℙ¹ over the origin in the second test) is excluded

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nashModification.lift
targets.statement: For h : Z → X with Z reduced, h⁻¹(U) dense, and a locally free rank-r quotient h^*F → M, there is a unique q : Z → N(X, F, r, U) with π_N ∘ q = h and q^*L_F = M as quotients, and M is the only such quotient of h^*F.
hypotheses: hypotheses of 1.2 with X reduced, locally Noetherian, U dense
h^*F → M surjective, M locally free of rank r

locator.where: Section 3, lines 226–229, and Section 2, lines 153–162; gonzalezSprinberg1982 §1.2, lines 94–98

tests.name: lift_id

tests.statement: over 𝔽_p(t), k(s) has degree p² over its p-th powers, not p

targets.name: exists_pMonomialOperators
targets.statement: For a local k-algebra R of characteristic p with x_j ∈ m and derivations ∂_i, ∂_i(x_j) = δ_ij, there are R^p-linear operators φ_γ (γ ∈ {0,…,p−1}^d) with φ_γ(x^β) = δ_{γβ}, built from (α!)⁻¹ ∂^α and the inverse of the unitriangular matrix (∂^{(α)}(x^β)).

locator.where: proof of Theorem 3.10, lines 271–283; nashModificationNotes2024 lines 394–407

tests.name: pMonomial_d0
tests.statement: d = 0: φ = id

tests.name: pMonomial_cusp_char3
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 3: operators exist but y = t³ is not in the R³-span of 1, x, x²

targets.name: frobeniusBasis_functionField
targets.statement: For k perfect of characteristic p, K finitely generated over k with dim Ω_{K/k} = d and dx_1, …, dx_d a basis, the monomials x^α (α ∈ {0,…,p−1}^d) form a K^p-basis of K; [K : K^p] = p^d.

tests.name: frobeniusBasis_rational

tests.name: frobeniusBasis_finite
tests.statement: d = 0: K perfect, basis {1}

tests.name: frobeniusBasis_tp_not_basis
tests.statement: t^p has zero differential and is not a p-basis of k(t)

targets.name: frobeniusPushforward_free_of_kaehler_surjection
targets.statement: For k perfect of characteristic p, X normal, of finite type, pure of dimension d, x closed, R = O_{X,x} and q : Ω_{R/k} → R^d surjective, ψ : ⊕_α R e_α → F_*R, e_α ↦ x^α, is an isomorphism; hence Frobenius is flat and R is regular.

tests.name: psi_cusp_char3

tests.name: psi_point
tests.statement: d = 0, R = k: ψ is the identity

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nashBlowupHom_isIso_iff_smooth_of_normal
targets.statement: For a perfect field k of characteristic p > 0 and X normal in the Setting, ν is an isomorphism iff X is smooth over k.

tests.name: imperfect_regular_curve
tests.statement: over 𝔽_p(t), x^p + y² + t = 0 is regular, not smooth, and ν is an isomorphism (stacksAlgebra Example 10.140.8, 00TY)

tests.name: cusp_small_char

tests.name: quadric_cone
tests.statement: z² = xy in characteristic p ≠ 2: J = (x, y, z) not invertible, ν not an isomorphism

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizedNashBlowup
targets.statement: X̄* is the normalisation of X* (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §5.4) with η : X̄* → X* and ν̄ = ν ∘ η.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over k

locator.where: Introduction, lines 20–21; gonzalezSprinberg1982 lines 60–69; stacksNormalization Definition 29.55.1 (035N) line 6498, Lemma 29.55.3 (035P) line 6521

api.name: normalizedNashBlowup.isFinite
api.statement: η is finite, surjective, birational on components and an isomorphism over the normal locus of X*, in particular over ν⁻¹(X_sm)

api.name: normalizedNashBlowup_setting
api.statement: X̄* is normal, separated, of finite type, pure of dimension d, with dense smooth locus

api.name: normalizedNashBlowupHom_isModification
api.statement: ν̄ is proper, an isomorphism over X_sm, with ν̄⁻¹(X_sm) dense

tests.name: normalized_cusp_char0
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 0: X̄* = X* = 𝔸¹

tests.name: normalized_cusp_char2
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2: X* ≅ X, X̄* = 𝔸¹

tests.name: normalized_vs_normalization
tests.statement: y² = x²z in characteristic ≠ 2: the normalisation of X is finite over X, while X̄* = X* has ℙ¹ over 0; normalising X instead of X* is excluded (in characteristic 2, J_f = (x²) is invertible and X* = X)

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizedNashBlowup.lift
targets.statement: For X in the Setting, Z locally Noetherian and normal, h : Z → X sending generic points of components to generic points, and a locally free rank-d quotient of h^*Ω_{X/k}, there is a unique Z → X̄* over X compatible with the quotients.
hypotheses: h maps generic points of components of Z to generic points of components of X

tests.name: lift_self
tests.statement: Z = X̄*: the lift is the identity

tests.name: lift_cusp_char2
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2 with Z = 𝔸¹: the lift is 𝔸¹ ≅ X̄*

tests.name: lift_closed_point
tests.statement: a closed point of X_sm does not map a generic point to a generic point; outside the hypotheses

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizedNashBlowup.baseChange
targets.statement: For V ⊆ X open, V̄* ≅ ν̄⁻¹(V); for a finite separable extension k'/k, (X̄*)_{k'} ≅ (X_{k'})̄* over X_{k'}.

tests.name: restrict_smooth
tests.statement: V = X_sm: V̄* = V

tests.name: cusp_Qi
tests.statement: cusp over ℚ, k' = ℚ(i): both sides 𝔸¹

tests.name: inseparable_fails
tests.statement: C : x^p + y² + t = 0 over 𝔽_p(t): C̄* = C but (C_{k'})̄* = 𝔸¹ ≠ C_{k'} for k' = k(t^{1/p})

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizedNashBlowupHom_isIso_iff
targets.statement: For X in the Setting, ν̄ is an isomorphism iff X is normal and ν is an isomorphism; hence in characteristic zero, and over a perfect field of characteristic p, ν̄ is an isomorphism iff X is smooth.
hypotheses: for the corollary: char k = 0, or k perfect

tests.name: cusp_char2_normalized_not_iso
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2: ν iso, X not normal, ν̄ not iso

tests.name: smooth_both_iso
tests.statement: X smooth: both isomorphisms

tests.name: imperfect_regular_curve_normalized
tests.statement: x^p + y² + t = 0 over 𝔽_p(t): ν̄ iso, not smooth

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.normalizedNashIterate
targets.statement: Y_0 = X, Y_{i+1} = (Y_i)̄*; NormalizedNashIterationResolves X d means some Y_i → Spec k is smooth; if X is smooth, X^{(i)} ≅ X ≅ Y_i for all i.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over k

api.name: normalizedNashIterate_zero / _succ
api.statement: Y_0 = X, Y_{i+1} = normalizedNashBlowup of Y_i

api.name: normalizedNashIterate_setting
api.statement: for X in the Setting each Y_i (i ≥ 1) is normal and in the Setting

api.name: nashIterate_of_smooth / normalizedNashIterate_of_smooth
api.statement: X smooth implies X^{(i)} ≅ X ≅ Y_i over X

tests.name: normalizedIterate_cusp_char0
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 0: Y_1 = 𝔸¹

tests.name: normalizedIterate_cusp_char2
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2: Y_1 = 𝔸¹ smooth while X^{(i)} ≅ X

tests.name: normalizedIterate_zero
tests.statement: Y_0 = X, normal or not

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.iterate_openSubscheme
targets.statement: For Y in the Setting, U ⊆ Y open and a k-isomorphism U ≅ Z, the i-th (normalised) Nash iterate of Y contains an open subscheme k-isomorphic to that of Z; so if Y_m ⊇ U ≅ X with m ≥ 1, then Y_{m+i} contains a copy of Y_i and Y_{jm} a copy of X for all j ≥ 1, and likewise for X^{(i)}.

tests.name: open_self
tests.statement: U = Y: identity

tests.name: cusp_char2_copies
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2: X^{(j)} ⊇ X for all j

tests.name: smoothLocus_iterates
tests.statement: U = Y_sm: the iterates of U are U

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_normalizedNashIterationResolves_of_openSubscheme
targets.statement: If X is in the Setting and singular and for some m ≥ 1 the iterate Y_m (resp. X^{(m)}) contains an open subscheme k-isomorphic to X, then no Y_i (resp. X^{(i)}) is smooth over k.
hypotheses: an open subscheme of Y_m (resp. X^{(m)}) k-isomorphic to X

tests.name: m_zero_fails
tests.statement: m = 0: the hypothesis always holds and the cusp in characteristic 0 is resolved

tests.name: smooth_excluded
tests.statement: X smooth: singularity hypothesis fails, Y_0 smooth

tests.name: cusp_char2_nash
tests.statement: cusp in characteristic 2, m = 1, Nash iteration: never smooth; normalised iteration resolved since Y_1 = 𝔸¹ has no open copy of X

suppliers.what: coherentGrassmannian with universal quotient, classifying maps, base change and properness over an affine base; plucker; normalisation of reduced schemes (scheme case of DMNormalization.stack) with universal property, finiteness over Nagata bases and smooth base change; schematic closure commuting with flat base change.

dimension theory of finite-type k-schemes; descent of smoothness along field extensions; bijective_of_depth; universal homeomorphisms; normal schemes and DVR codimension-one stalks; modifications with witness; regularLocus_eq_smoothLocus over a perfect field and Serre's normality criterion.

p-bases of fields: a family is a p-basis exactly when its differentials form a basis of Ω¹_{K/𝔽_p}; the forward half is DerivedDeRham.pBasis_kaehler_basis, the converse half (used by §5.3) is stated in the prose of §0.23.
exists_lieDerivativeOneForm / lieDerivativeOneForm: the unique C-linear Lie derivative on Ω[F⁄C] for fields C ⊆ F with C of characteristic zero; used only for the agreement bullet of §4.2.

consumers.what: Proposed Part II: higher-order Nash blowups (principal parts), normalised Nash transformations of surfaces, the Fitting-ideal comparison; consumes §§1.2–1.5, Layer 2 and Layer 6.
